instructions: The night before, or at least 2 hours ahead: rinse the 1 cup urad dal and 1/4 cup chana dal together a few times, until the water runs mostly clear. Cover them with about 3 cups fresh water and leave them to soak for at least 2 hours. If they're soaking overnight, keep the bowl in the fridge.
Seed and finely chop the green chili and finely chop the ginger. Finely chop the leaves from 1 sprig of curry leaves and 1 tbsp of the cilantro.

Drain the dals in a sieve and shake off as much water as you can. Put them in a blender with 2 tbsp cold water. Blend, stopping often to scrape down the sides, and add more cold water only a teaspoon at a time if the blades stall. Stop when the batter is smooth and very thick. A runny batter won't hold a ring shape.

Transfer the batter into a bowl and beat it with your hand in one direction for about 1 minute, until it looks lighter. Drop a small blob into a cup of water. If it floats, it's ready. If it sinks, beat it for another minute.
Stir in the chili, ginger, curry leaves, cilantro, 3 tbsp of the coconut, 2 tsp of the rice flour, the pinch of hing and the 3/4 tsp salt.

Pour the 4 cups oil into a heavy pot. It should be about 2 inches deep. Heat it over medium to 350°F. If you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Drop in a pea of batter. It should rise to the top steadily with small bubbles around it, without browning straight away.

Set a bowl of water next to you and wet your hands. Take a lump of batter about the size of a golf ball, set it on your wet palm and flatten it a little. Wet your thumb and push a hole through the middle.
Slide it gently off your fingers into the oil, close to the surface. Stand back a little. It can spatter. Shape and add 2 or 3 more, without crowding the pot.

Fry them for 2 to 3 minutes, until the undersides are golden. Flip them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're deep golden and crisp. If they brown faster than that, turn the heat down a touch, or the middles stay raw.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto paper towels. Fry the rest the same way, wetting your hands each time. You'll get about 12.
Serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.
advance_prep_notes: Soak the dals at least 2 hours ahead, or overnight in the fridge.
method_notes: Both versions soak urad dal for a few hours, grind it to a thick batter with as little water as possible, stir in green chili, ginger and curry leaves, shape wet-handed rings with a hole in the middle and fry them golden in oil that's hot but not fierce. Hebbar's Kitchen grinds a little chana dal in with the urad and adds dried coconut, cilantro, rice flour for crispness and a pinch of hing. Swasthi's uses urad dal alone with cumin and crushed pepper, grinds it with ice cold water, and beats the batter until a blob floats in water. This follows Hebbar's batter and amounts, about 12 vadas, with Swasthi's beating and float test, and one seeded chili so it stays mild.
